pr_title: Allow more than one KNN search clause
pr_body:
It makes sense to allow more than one KNN search clause per individual search request. It may be that different documents have separate vector spaces or that a single doc is index with more than one vector space. In both of these scenarios, users may want to retrieve a resulting set that takes into account all their indexed vector spaces. 

A prime example here would be searching a semantic text embedding along with searching an image embedding. 


closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/91187

issue_context.title: Extend `knn` section to support multiple fields
comments: @benwtrent , do you plan to support `boost` to each field in `knn` ? TIA !!

@nirmalc Gotta think on this a bit more :). There are some other things in flight that may have knock on effects here.

But, I do think individual boosts per field make sense. You would want to boost title over body, for example.

Just for completion's sake, another possible way for this to look (which I don't particularly like) is:

```json
{
  "knn": {
    "field": ["image-vector","caption-vector"],
    "query_vector": [[-5, 9, -12], [0.91, -0.21, 0.43]],
    "k": [10, 10],
    "num_candidates": [50, 100],
    "boost": [1, 2.0]
  },
  "fields": [ "title", "file-type" ]
}
```

Downsides here are:
 - API needs to validate that all these array values are the same size
 - Not as intuitive as simply supplying multiple configuration objects
 - If one configuration is changed, the other MUST be provided (e.g. no easy way for one vector search to have "default" values where the others are provided).

@nirmalc I have had the same thoughts. The downside there is the assumption that all fields are within the same vector space. There is a real use-case behind being able to query an "image embedding" and a "text embedding" in different vector spaces with separate query vectors (originating from the same text).

So, I suppose, I see the use of BOTH syntaxes. Your suggestion could be considered syntactic sugar for @jtibshirani's design when the vector fields are in the same space.
I agree with @benwtrent that the first approach should be the original design. If there's enough demand then we can add the second approach as syntactic sugar as a follow up.

review_comments: I can see how this could be controversial. But I don't really see the need in pushing down potentially a bunch of duplicate score docs. We COULD allow them to be linearly combined within the Lucene query somehow, but that would then require some change within `KnnScoreDocQuery` to handle duplicate docs. It just seemed saner to do it up here.
I tend to agree
could we make this final? instead of taking a list we could take KnnSearchBuilders and add to the initial list internally
@javanna none of the other list field values behave this way. I would rather have consistency so as not to create surprises.
shall we open an issue so we don't forget to look into running these queries concurrently rather than sequentially?
is it worth testing aggregations too when multiple vector queries are provided, just to double check?
I will add agg checks to both new tests :)
Good test! Super happy to see this.

@benwtrent This seems like the best solution to me for the most part for profiling. The only thing I'm concerned about is the rewrite time is combined (if I'm looking at this output correctly) for all knn searches. I wonder if that should be split per knn query as I think it would be useful to know which particular knn query is taking the most time.
We could serialize a `List<QueryProfileShardResult>`. I would have to add some BWC serialization logic to make sure we don't break things.
That makes sense to me if it's not a huge amount of work to add. Otherwise, as a work around a user can profile the individual knn queries as separate queries to get the breakdown.
